cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Successful Compliance
cards.instruction: Describe a failed outcome as proof that the correct process was followed and therefore the system worked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The wedding cake collapsed, but our final inspection caught it. The system worked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Exactly. No defective cake reached a guest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The couple want a refund for the entire cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which matches our rejection of the entire cake. I'll record that as full customer agreement with quality control.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 certifies system success, A3 rules no serving is protection, A5 determines how refund is officially recorded; authority defines failure as successful process.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 nothing to serve causes A3 no defect served; B4 full refund causes A5 total rejection agreement.

relationship.evidence: B2 names the actual service failure and B4 client demand, a plausible colleague dealing with consequences.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 customer rejection as another sign-off on quality control, extending the false success judgment.

specificity.evidence: A1 collapsed wedding cake and inspection, B4 couple refund make the failed service unambiguous.
